answer: A claim is not paid when it lands. It is carved into the onyx ledger and lit by a beacon for two hours, open to objections proving a duplicate. A dune warden drawn at random checks each objection in the public record. An unchallenged claim clears; a proven duplicate is a buried claim: payment void, barred a week. Five cents and one real job buy a clear window; a farmer with 1,000 fakes must defend 1,000 windows and risks 1,000 exposed duplicates.
